summary: Iter 79 — Phase 3 Store & Inventory (Material Request + 2-step Transfer + Site/Project views) tested end-to-end. Backend: 30/30 new HTTP API tests pass (after 1 bug fix). 7/7 unit tests pass. Phase 1 (Iter 77) + Phase 2 (Iter 78) regression: 35/35 pass — total 72 PASSED, 2 SKIPPED, 0 FAILED. Fixed a critical 500 error in POST /api/inv3/material-requests/{id}/issue where Mongo's ObjectId leaked into the response (FastAPI couldn't JSON-serialize). Material Request lifecycle works: submitted → approved → partially_issued → issued; reject after approval blocked; self-approve blocked for non-super_admin (verified by source); approved-balance/insufficient-stock/item-not-in-MR all return 400. Transfer 2-step works: dispatch posts transfer_out + debits source + status=in_transit; receive validates received+shortage+damaged≤dispatched, requires remarks/attachment on shortage, credits destination, sets status=received_with_exception. Aggregations site-stock/project-stock/project-consumption return correct shape with date filter respected. Pending-returnable surfaces outstanding allocations with outstanding_qty/value/days_out/overdue. Project-closure-check correctly blocks closure when pending_returnable>0 / in_transit>0 / pending_mr>0 and reports can_close=true for clean project. Frontend: All 8 new sidebar testids (si-nav-material_req / material_trf / in_transit / returnable / site_stock / project_stock / project_consumption / closure_check) render under 'Material Movement' and 'Project & Site' groups. All 8 views load without console errors. Closure check has closure-project + closure-run + closure-result testids. Phase 1/2 regression intact in sidebar (dashboard, categories, stores, opening_stock, settings, pr_from_stock, pending_pos, pipeline all present).

minor.issue: Was returning HTTP 500 'ObjectId not iterable' because alloc_doc retained Mongo _id after insert_one. FIXED by alloc_doc.pop('_id', None) immediately after insert_one. Re-tested: 28/28 pass.

action_items: (verify) Confirm Phase 3 fix on routers/inventory_phase3_router.py L278 (alloc_doc.pop('_id', None)) is acceptable — it is the same MongoDB ObjectId hygiene applied elsewhere in the codebase and prevents 500s when /issue allocations are returned.

(optional, low) MR auto-numbering uses count_documents (same race concern flagged in Iter 77/78) — acceptable for v1; consider an atomic counters collection or unique index on mr_number before high-concurrency rollout.
(optional, low) Transfer transfer_no also uses count_documents and same numbering pattern — same recommendation.
(optional, low) issue_from_mr swallows accounting_service.post_stock_issue errors with bare except — log the error at WARN level so accounting reconciliation gaps are not silent.

(optional, low) project-closure-check counts in_transit by project_code only — if a transfer has no project_code tagged, it won't block project closure even if the destination/source is at that site. Document or surface this as a separate 'untagged transfers' warning.
critical_code_review_comments: inventory_phase3_router.py L277 (now L278): MUST pop _id after insert_one to avoid 500 — FIXED in this iteration.

issue_from_mr (L213): the entire issue loop is NOT wrapped in a transaction. If one line's inventory.update_one succeeds but a later line fails, source stock is already debited for the earlier line(s) and partial allocation rows persist. Acceptable for v1 (rare with single-user flow) but consider Mongo multi-document transactions for production.

approve_mr (L155): role bypass `super_admin/director` for self-approve is correct, but director is also in the allowed-roles set at L147 — verify the spec really wants director to be able to self-approve (current code: yes).

create_transfer (L391): debits source inventory inside a loop BEFORE writing the transfer doc. If material_transfers.insert_one fails after some lines were debited, stock is silently lost. Consider build-then-write pattern or compensating debit-rollback on exception.

receive_transfer (L503): the shortage/damaged 'must have reason' check uses OR — allowing either damage_attachment_url OR received_remarks. Spec phrased 'damaged_attachment_url OR received_remarks' — current implementation matches. Confirm with PM if attachment is mandatory for damage > 0 (current: not enforced).
in_transit_stock (L562): age_days computed in Python from ISO string — works but a small Mongo aggregation would be more efficient at scale.

project-consumption (L632): only includes txn_type='outward'; transfers (transfer_out) are NOT counted as project consumption. Confirm this is by-design — transfers move stock between stores, not consume it.

rca of the issue: RCA — `/api/inv3/material-requests/{id}/issue` returning 500: motor's `insert_one(alloc_doc)` mutates the passed dict by adding the generated `_id` (ObjectId) field. The handler then appended the same dict to its `allocations` response array. FastAPI's `jsonable_encoder` cannot serialize bson.ObjectId → ValueError. REPRODUCTION: create MR with 2 lines, approve, POST /issue with valid lines → 500. MITIGATION: add `alloc_doc.pop('_id', None)` immediately after `await db.material_allocations.insert_one(alloc_doc)` so the dict appended to `allocations` no longer has the ObjectId. Same pattern is already used at L134 for the MR doc. Fix verified: 28/28 MR + transfer tests pass.
